premises.text: People buy brand clothes because they want to talk about them and show what they wear
premises.evidence_span: They want to talk about them. They want others get to know what they have, what they wear

premises.text: Spotting a desirable item on someone creates demand to identify the brand and where to buy it
premises.evidence_span: It's a common situation when you see somebody, for example, in a cafe wearing with gorgeous shoes, and you realize you want the same one

premises.text: The brand-in tag is a Foursquare-style check-in that labels brands on photos
premises.evidence_span: If you want, it's like in Foursquare, you check in places. In a tag brand, you brand in in brands

premises.text: The iPhone app lets the community identify brands from photos and deliver purchase advice through fast polls
premises.evidence_span: TechBrand's iPhone app helps you to make the right choice

premises.text: The web service unites people around brand loyalty with tagging tools, wardrobes, and wish lists, extended across the web by a browser bookmarklet
premises.evidence_span: It provides them with the tools for tagging brands on their photos and even on photos from social networks like Facebook

premises.text: Brands will pay to communicate with their own fans and with competitors' fans
premises.evidence_span: Brands will love it. And they will pay us for it

premises.text: A store marketplace auto-attaches links to brandings by analyzing keywords from store price lists
premises.evidence_span: Stores provide us with a price list and our system analyze keywords and automatically attach the links to the branding

value.text: Brand lovers satisfy their curiosity and show, identify, and shop the brands around them
value.evidence_span: All you need in this situation is just to run our iPhone app and ask community what brand it is by making a question branding

causal_links.evidence_span: you will get the right choice. The choice making has never been so fast
we are creating special marketplace for stores which appears in a branding area

notes: Three domains with an explicit justification, not a habit template: the consumer-behavior premises (D1) are independently testable assumptions about brand display and curiosity; the tag/app/web-service product (D2) revises on product usage; monetization (D3) revises on brand and store willingness to pay — each could fail while the others hold. The bookmarklet is folded into the web-service premise as an extension of the same tagging mechanism per v1.3.2 clarification 5. Investment ask and team experience excluded per 4.2. ASR noise ('brand in', 'BookMarket') normalized silently in premise text. No plainly asserted premise-prerequisite.
